title: 6 best AI logo generators for editable, usable brand assets
summary: Compare six AI logo generators by editable SVGs, design controls, brand kits, downloads and rights. Includes a fair test, prompt and production checklist.
body_markdown:
The best AI logo generator depends on the file you need after the preview. Use Recraft when an editable SVG is the starting requirement, Canva or Adobe Express when you want a familiar design editor, Looka for a packaged brand kit, Kittl for typography-heavy customization, or Magic Hour to explore distinctive logo concepts from a prompt. A polished preview is not yet a production-ready brand asset.

Magic Hour publishes this guide and is included in the comparison. The recommendations describe documented workflow fit, not a controlled ranking of design quality. Official product pages were checked September 12, 2026.


### Generate a logo direction from your brief


Describe the brand, symbol, palette, geometry, and typography. Generate several concepts, then verify spelling, small-size legibility, originality, and the files you need before launch.


[Try AI Logo Generator](https://magichour.ai/tools/ai-logo-generator)


## The file test that matters most


Before comparing styles, decide whether you need a raster image or an editable vector. PNG and JPG files are pixel-based. An SVG uses scalable paths and is usually easier to resize for a favicon, sign, or package without soft edges. A PDF may contain vector content, but the file extension alone does not guarantee that every element is editable.


Also separate a generated image from a logo system. A usable delivery normally needs horizontal, stacked, symbol-only, black, white, color, and transparent variants; spacing rules; exact color values; font information; and files that another designer or printer can open.


## 1. Magic Hour: prompt-based logo concepts


[Magic Hour AI Logo Generator](https://magichour.ai/tools/ai-logo-generator) accepts a written logo brief, offers style directions, and returns image variations without requiring sign-up for the first use. The page positions the workflow as rapid logo and brand-mark exploration across several image models.


Choose it when you want to explore symbols, emblems, mascots, or visual directions quickly. Treat lettering and exact geometry as drafts: verify every character, rebuild exact type where needed, and vectorize the selected mark before using it at many sizes. The current logo page does not document native editable SVG output.


## 2. Recraft: direct editable SVG generation


[Recraft AI Vector Generator](https://www.recraft.ai/ai-vector-generator) documents direct text-to-SVG output, editable paths and layers, palette changes, resizing, and export without loss of edge sharpness. It also supports converting an existing raster image to SVG.


Choose it when a vector is required from the start. Inspect the generated paths rather than trusting the file extension: reduce unnecessary nodes, correct overlaps, convert or replace lettering, and test the mark in one color and at favicon size.


## 3. Canva: template-led logo design and collaboration


[Canva Logo Maker](https://www.canva.com/create/logos/) combines customizable logo templates, an AI logo route, drag-and-drop editing, icons, type, colors, collaboration, mockups, and downloads. Its official page lists PNG, JPEG, and PDF among the output choices.


Choose it when non-designers need to edit and reuse a mark across social graphics, presentations, or print layouts. Check the exact plan for Brand Kit, resizing, transparent-background, and vector-export requirements rather than assuming every Canva feature is free.


## 4. Adobe Express: generated concepts plus an editor


[Adobe Express AI Logo Generator](https://www.adobe.com/express/create/ai/logo) creates concepts from a prompt, can use style or composition references, and opens results in the Express editor for added text and graphics. The current AI logo page documents a transparent PNG download.


Choose it when you want prompt generation and a broader design editor in the same workflow. If a printer or designer requires SVG, EPS, or fully editable paths, verify the specific export route before building the rest of the brand around the generated asset.


## 5. Looka: logo files and a packaged brand kit


[Looka Logo Maker](https://looka.com/logo-maker/) starts with a company name, industry, styles, colors, and symbols, then generates designs to customize. Looka’s current pricing page separates a one-time logo purchase from annual Brand Kit subscriptions.


Choose it when the handoff should include coordinated social, stationery, and brand assets. Looka says Premium Logo and qualifying Brand Kit packages include high-resolution files, transparent variations, SVG, EPS, PDF, and PNG. Previewing is free, but downloading and using the files requires a purchase.


## 6. Kittl: typography and layout refinement


[Kittl AI Logo Generator](https://www.kittl.com/tools/ai-logo-generator) combines generation from brand inputs with an editor for fonts, colors, icons, layouts, text effects, and typography. Its current page lists PNG, JPG, PDF, and SVG downloads and a token-based free starting allowance after sign-up.


Choose it when type treatment is a central part of the mark. Confirm the current plan and licensing terms for the fonts, elements, AI generations, and SVG export used in the final design.


## A fair 20-minute logo-generator test


1.


Use one fictional brand to avoid copying a real mark: name, audience, personality, industry, and three attributes.


2.


Ask for one symbol-led direction and one wordmark direction using the same palette and constraints in every compatible tool.


3.


Record sign-up, generation allowance, editing controls, exact download formats, transparent background, vector access, licensing terms, and total price to obtain usable files.


4.


Test the chosen mark at 16 pixels, 32 pixels, social-avatar size, website-header size, black and white, and on both light and dark backgrounds.


5.


Inspect spelling, letterforms, negative space, symmetry, path quality, similarity to known brands, and whether another designer can edit the delivered file.


## Reusable AI logo prompt


Create a simple \[symbol, wordmark, monogram, or emblem\] for \[fictional brand name\], a \[industry\] brand for \[audience\]. The personality is \[three adjectives\]. Use \[two colors\] on a plain background, bold clean geometry, strong negative space, and a silhouette that remains clear at 16 pixels. Avoid gradients, mockups, extra objects, tiny details, stock-style icons, slogans, and resemblance to existing brands. Generate the symbol without text first.


Generating the symbol without text helps separate image quality from lettering accuracy. Add the exact brand name in an editor with a licensed font, then create the required lockups and spacing rules.


## Production-ready logo checklist


-


The name is spelled correctly and uses a font you are allowed to use.


-


The symbol is recognizable in one color and at 16- and 32-pixel sizes.


-


Horizontal, stacked, symbol-only, black, white, color, and transparent versions exist.


-


The delivery includes SVG or another appropriate vector file when scaling and editing are required.


-


Raster exports have enough resolution for their intended digital or print use.


-


Colors and spacing are documented, and the mark works on light and dark backgrounds.


-


A similarity and trademark search has been completed in every market where the brand will operate.


-


A human reviews the final design for cultural meaning, accessibility, originality, and legal risk.


## Frequently asked questions


###


Use Recraft for direct editable SVG generation, Canva or Adobe Express for familiar editing, Looka for a packaged brand kit, Kittl for typography-heavy customization, and Magic Hour for fast prompt-based concept exploration. The best choice is the one that delivers the files and editing path your real brand requires.


###


Provider permission is only one part of the decision. Check the selected plan’s commercial terms, font and stock-asset licenses, similarity to existing marks, and the copyright and trademark rules in your jurisdiction. Do not assume a generated image is exclusive or automatically protectable.


###


An SVG is useful when the logo must scale cleanly and another designer needs editable paths. You may still need PNG files for websites and social profiles, plus PDF or EPS files for particular printers and production partners.


###


Image generators can distort letters or produce inconsistent wordmarks. Adding the exact name in an editor gives you control over spelling, font licensing, kerning, alignment, and repeatable lockups.


###


Search the symbol, name, and similar marks before launch, then run the appropriate trademark search for your markets and classes. A provider calling an output unique does not replace legal clearance or prove exclusivity.
